review_notes: Read all 652 lines of the target plus the `CauchyPrincipalValue'`/`CauchyPrincipalValueExists'` definitions in `.../GeneralizedResidueTheory/Basic.lean` (lines 64–95), and checked how the target's results are consumed in `.../Residue/SectorCurveLemma.lean` (lines 520–535, 857–864). I verified the mathematics of the PV computation by hand: segment 1 gives ∫_δ^1 dt/t = -log δ, segment 2 gives iα, segment 3 gives ∫_2^{3-δ} -dt/(3-t) = log δ, so the cutoff integral is iα and the limit exists; the statements `pv_integrand_seg1/2/3`, `sectorCurve_norm_seg1/seg3'`, `log_cancellation`, `pv_sector_cutoff_eq` and the derivative lemmas all check out at the endpoints and for degenerate angles (α = 0 traces out and back with PV 0 = i·0; α = 2π gives 2πi). I found no statement that is vacuously true, has an empty domain, or contradicts its docstring, so the only defect fitting this rubric is the one filed: the headline theorem carries an undocumented, unused angle restriction that misrepresents the requirement for the PV to exist. Two further declarations have the same (milder) vestigial-hypothesis pattern - `integral_seg1_eq_neg_log` and `integral_seg3_eq_log` (lines 254–268) require `_hε1 : ε < 1`, although e.g. ε = 2 also satisfies ∫_2^1 t⁻¹ = -Real.log 2; I did not file these separately to avoid duplicating a single class of issue. Uncertainty: the suggested removal of the `α`-hypotheses in `pv_sector_dz_over_z` (and in its call sites in SectorCurveLemma.lean) has not been compiled; I only verified that the proof body never mentions them and that the no-angle-hypothesis lemma `pv_sector_cutoff_eq` supplies the whole computation. Junk values of `sectorCurve` for t > 3 were noted and are harmless since no declaration in the file refers to t outside [0,3].

theorem pv_sector_dz_over_z (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (α : ℝ)
    (_hα_nonneg : 0 ≤ α) (_hα_le : α ≤ 2 * Real.pi) :
findings.problem: The headline result of the file is stated only for sector opening angles `α` with `0 ≤ α ≤ 2*Real.pi`, but these two hypotheses are never used: they are bound with underscore names and the proof body (lines 632–650) refers only to `hr`, deriving everything from `pv_sector_cutoff_eq r hr α ε hε_pos (mem_Iio.mp hε)`. Since `pv_sector_cutoff_eq` (line 578) already holds for every real `α` (it proves the cutoff integral equals `I * α` for arbitrary `α`, with no angle hypothesis), the existence of the principal value and its value `I * α` are true for angles outside [0, 2π] as well. Concretely, with `α = 3 * Real.pi` the truncated integral is still `3 * Real.pi * I` and the limit exists, yet this cannot be obtained from `pv_sector_dz_over_z` as stated. The docstring (lines 624–626) says only 'The principal value of `dz/z` along the sector curve from 0 to 3 equals `I * alpha`' and never mentions an angle restriction, so a reader is left to infer that PV existence is angle-dependent (as it is for the winding-number interpretation downstream), which the statement does not support. The unused hypothesis also propagates: `SectorCurveLemma.cauchyPV_sectorCurve_simplePole` and `generalizedWindingNumber_sectorCurve` both pass `hα_nonneg hα_le` through to this lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the two unused binders `(_hα_nonneg : 0 ≤ α) (_hα_le : α ≤ 2 * Real.pi)` from `pv_sector_dz_over_z` (the proof already never mentions them and every ingredient, in particular `pv_sector_cutoff_eq`, is free of angle hypotheses), and drop the corresponding arguments at the call sites in `SectorCurveLemma.lean` (`cauchyPV_sectorCurve_simplePole`, `cauchyPV_sectorCurve_eq_mul_residueSimplePole`, `generalizedWindingNumber_sectorCurve`). If instead the restriction is meant to record the paper's sector convention, keep it only where it is semantically needed (the winding-number statement, where `α/(2π)` must be a genuine winding number) and state explicitly in the docstring of `pv_sector_dz_over_z` that the hypotheses are not needed for the identity. This has not been compiled; it relies only on the observation that the tactic proof never uses the hypotheses.
findings.benefit: Users get the identity at full strength (PV of `dz/z` along the model sector curve is `I * α` for every real `α`), matching what the proof and the no-angle-hypothesis cutoff lemma actually establish, and the docstring no longer appears contradicted by the signature. Downstream sector lemmas then need not carry an unnecessary angle constraint, and readers are not misled into thinking the principal value only exists for facing angles in [0, 2π].
